instruction: Please set up my AOL email account in Thunderbird with email address "vintage.mail2024@aol.com" and password 'aol_vintage_99' (without quotes). Ignore any authentication or connection failure warnings. Just complete the account setup and I'll manually verify the settings afterward.

metadata.explanation: Task variation for AOL Mail account setup in Thunderbird. Evaluator verifies IMAP (imap.aol.com) and SMTP (smtp.aol.com) account configurations with correct credentials.

llm_judge_reasons: Critical semantic mismatch between instruction and evaluator verification logic
Instruction explicitly tells users to 'ignore any authentication or connection failure warnings' and 'just complete the account setup', implying authentication may fail
Evaluator uses firefox_decrypt.py to extract saved credentials, which only works if Thunderbird successfully authenticated and saved the credentials to the profile
If authentication fails (as instruction suggests), Thunderbird will not save credentials, firefox_decrypt.py will find nothing, and evaluator will fail even if user correctly configured the account
This creates a false negative: user follows instructions correctly, but evaluator cannot detect the configuration because it depends on successful authentication
The evaluator verifies authentication success (saved credentials) rather than configuration correctness (server settings, email, username)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Modify instruction to require successful authentication (remove 'ignore authentication failures' language)
OR: Change evaluator to verify account configuration from Thunderbird's prefs.js/accounts config files (which store settings regardless of auth success)
OR: Use accessibility tree or UI inspection to verify account settings are present in Thunderbird's account manager
The evaluator logic (check_csv + firefox_decrypt) is correct for verifying saved credentials, but incompatible with an instruction that allows authentication failures
